summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR174 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.9% as raw material cost pass-through lagged.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a margin-compressed quarter: revenue grew 18% YoY and 8% QoQ to INR174 crore, while gross margin fell to 34.3% and EBITDA margin to 7.9%. Management attributed this to a fresh input-cost spike from the West Asia conflict, export orders priced before the spike, and a deliberate choice to absorb part of the cost increase for long-standing customers. Working capital rose sharply, inventory to INR120.2 crore and receivables to INR100.1 crore, and H1 operating cash flow was negative. Management says the shipment backlog and receivables are unwinding into Q3 and guides to 15-20% FY27 revenue growth and 7-8% volume growth.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic revenue grew about 36% QoQ and 27% YoY, lifting its share to 19.5% from 15.5% in Q1. 36 new customers were added in H1 and a new Hydration range of bottles and jars was launched. Management says domestic gross margin is 12-13 points above export.

segments.name: Exports - United States
segments.commentary: US contributed about 10% of revenue in Q2 versus about 19% in Q1, which management attributes to shipment timing. A US stationery customer is expected to roughly double business as products move into its core range, and to become the second-largest customer by end-FY27.

segments.name: Exports - European Union and UK
segments.commentary: EU contributed about 59% of revenue and UK about 10%. Largest customer contribution was 59% per the Q&A. October sales were described as encouraging.

segments.name: Bamboo (subsidiary All Time Bamboo Pvt Ltd, Guwahati)
segments.commentary: Guwahati facility is fully installed, with commercial production from mid-November 2026 and revenue expected from Q4 FY27. Management guides about INR60 crore revenue at current installed capacity, and separately INR25-30 crore for CY27. Total capex to date about INR18 crore, targeted at INR20 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 15-20%, with management reiterating it on the call.
FY27 volume (production) growth of at least 7-8%, with at least 15,000 MT production targeted in H2 FY27 on the current order book.
Capacity utilisation will not reach 75% in Q4 FY27; management targets 75% by Q2 FY28.

Gross margin and EBITDA expected to improve in H2 as price increases are negotiated and fixed costs at Khatalwada and Bamboo are absorbed. Management said margins could be better than the 12-13% EBITDA range discussed if conditions normalise.
About INR8 crore sales-in-transit and roughly 500 MT of Q2 sales (per the Q&A) are expected to be recognised in Q3 FY27, along with the production of extra finished goods.
Working capital expected to unwind in H2 and operating cash flow to turn positive.
Bamboo facility expected to double, with about INR10-12 crore of additional machinery, once utilisation reaches about 50%; management said this could happen by end-FY28.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is about 41,000 tonnes currently. 14 injection moulding machines adding about 1,500 tonnes are expected in December 2026, taking capacity to about 42,500 MT, which management calls the peak for now.

Blow-moulding capability has been added within the existing plant for bottles and jars in PP, PET, PETg and Tritan, scalable with demand. SCADA-based real-time machine monitoring has been initiated at Khatalwada.

Further capex will be project-by-project for confirmed programmes. Bamboo commercial production starts mid-November 2026; split-processing model has boards made at Guwahati and value-add at Khatalwada.
Silvassa production was suspended for 3 days in September due to storage constraints.
demand_pricing: Average polymer prices rose 40-45%. Export prices are fixed at order and revisable only on new orders, so confirmed orders were honoured at agreed prices.
About 50% of the input-cost increase has been passed to non-IKEA/non-largest customers so far. Domestic price increase was to be rolled out from the second week of November.
Management said some customers are resisting price increases because they are benchmarking against Chinese prices.
Management flagged possible demand headwinds at higher price points for some articles, but said utilisation has improved and no dramatic demand fall is visible.
Container backlog for the largest customer fell from 126 to 32 40-foot containers. Inbound raw material transit rose to about 50 days from a historic 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR120 crore inventory is finished goods, and how much will be recognised in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods were INR42 crore at end-Q2, of which INR8 crore is sales-in-transit recognised in October. The INR15.4 crore change in inventory includes INR8 crore sales to be booked in October and INR7 crore of extra production.

qa_highlights.question: How will gross margin trend, and what is the domestic vs export margin gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins should rise once raw material prices fall or prices are renegotiated; domestic price increases are in process. The gross margin gap between domestic and export is about 12-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 see better gross margin than Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some pricing gains in Q3 and Q4, but not back to historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 volume outlook, and is H2 visibility strong?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 7-8% volume growth for FY27. Management says H2 visibility is strong, with at least 15,000 MT production targeted in H2 on the current order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Bamboo ramp slower than planned, and is there demand headwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described Bamboo as a discovery phase; Guwahati is ready, with European sales waiting on FSC certification over a few months. Management said there is no dramatic demand fall, but price-sensitive articles could see some headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost increase has been passed on, and will falling crude be a margin benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the 40-45% increase has been passed to most customers, with the largest customer and IKEA on rollover contracts. Management says customers have committed to recover lost margins as prices fall.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on customer price renegotiations, with about half the raw-material cost increase passed through so far and some customers pushing back against Chinese pricing.
Working capital: inventory of INR120.2 crore and receivables of INR100.1 crore must unwind in H2 for operating cash flow to turn positive; H1 operating cash flow was negative.
Shipping and container disruption: inbound transit around 50 days versus a historic 30 days, and the container backlog must clear as stated.
Fixed-cost absorption at Khatalwada and Bamboo, and whether utilisation moves from 67% toward the 75% target by Q2 FY28.
Concentration: largest customer contributed 59% of revenue, and US share fell to about 10%.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious on near-term margins, attributing the miss to external shocks and a deliberate choice to absorb costs; confident on H2 volume, order visibility and the long-term domestic and Bamboo story. Answers on Bamboo capex and demand headwinds were qualified, and management avoided firm timelines on price recovery.
key_quotes: Q2 FY '27 was among the most challenging quarters in the company's history.
The increase in working capital is temporary, and our inventory carries no slow-moving stocks.
We have consciously absorbed part of this cost increase to protect the long -standing customer relationships.
We expect a substantial portion of the working capital buildup to unwind during H2 as the shipment backlog clears and collections are realized.
So the EBITDA margin will definitely be much better in H2.
Second half visibility is very strong. Orders are also there.

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth held at 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%) and volume growth of at least 7-8% with 15,000 MT H2 production on the current order book; 14 injection machines (~1,500 MT) due Dec 2026 and Bamboo starting mid-Nov, but H1 revenue is only +9.7% so H2 must accelerate, and the 75% utilisation target slipped to Q2 FY28.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 7.9% in Q2 from 14.3% in Q1 as raw material rose to ~66% of revenue from ~60%, with about 50% of the 40-45% polymer price rise passed through so far; management expects H2 gross margin and EBITDA to improve but not back to historical levels.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 14 injection moulding machines adding ~1,500 MT (about 3.7% on ~41,000 MT installed) are due December 2026, and Bamboo Guwahati starts commercial production mid-November 2026, though utilisation is only 67%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides at least 7-8% FY27 production growth and at least 15,000 MT production in H2 on the current order book, versus 6,910 MT in Q2 and H1 revenue growth of only 9.7%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 67%, well below the 80% threshold, and new capex is to be project-by-project; Bamboo doubling (INR10-12 crore machinery) is conditional on about 50% utilisation, which management says could come by end-FY28.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of 15-20% was only held, H1 revenue growth is 9.7%, and utilisation target slipped to 75% by Q2 FY28 from an earlier pace.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 revenue growth is only 9.7% against a 15-20% FY27 target, so H2 must grow sharply, and the margin recovery depends on customer price renegotiations and containers/shipping normalising.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bamboo commercial production from mid-Nov 2026 with ~INR60 crore FY27 revenue at installed capacity, plus a blow-moulding range for bottles and jars already added and a Hydration range launched in domestic market.

rows.label: Inventory and receivables unwind in H2
rows.why: Inventory rose to INR120.2 crore from INR68.6 crore and receivables to INR100.1 crore from INR74.9 crore, with INR8 crore sales-in-transit and ~500 MT of Q2 sales expected to be recognised in Q3 and operating cash flow expected to turn positive.

rows.label: Domestic price increase and customer price recovery
rows.why: About 50% of the 40-45% polymer price increase is passed through so far, and the domestic price increase rolls out from the second week of November, though some customers are resisting against Chinese pricing.

rows.label: US stationery customer to double business
rows.why: The US customer is expected to roughly double business and become the second-largest customer by end-FY27, but US share fell to about 10% of Q2 revenue from about 19% in Q1, which management attributes to shipment timing.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 volume visibility, the domestic growth target of 30-35% and the Bamboo story, but cautious on near-term margins, avoided firm timelines on price recovery and qualified answers on Bamboo demand and capex; analysts pressed on the margin miss and the working-capital build
